Let them pay for the doctor and the X-ray.
Exactly, you definitely need a good doctor.
Katya, can you drive me to the X-ray?

examples.text: Точно, тебе обязательно нужен хороший врач.
examples.trans: Exactly, you definitely need a good doctor.

examples.text: Возвращайся сегодня вечером пораньше домой, хорошо?
examples.trans: Come home early this evening, alright?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она машину совсем не заметила.
examples.trans: She did not notice the car at all.

examples.text: Денис, дыши спокойно, сейчас вызовем скорую.
examples.trans: Denis, breathe calmly, we will call an ambulance now.

examples.text: Всё нормально, я просто конфетой подавился.
examples.trans: Everything is fine, I just choked on a candy.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'X-ray' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Пусть они оплачивают врача и рентген.
examples.trans: Let them pay for the doctor and the X-ray.

examples.text: Катя, можешь меня на рентген отвезти?
examples.trans: Katya, can you drive me to the X-ray?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Завтра мы точно победим!
examples.trans: Tomorrow we will definitely win!

examples.text: Точно, тебе обязательно нужен хороший врач.
examples.trans: Exactly, you definitely need a good doctor.

examples.text: Значит, мы точно уволены, терять больше нечего.
examples.trans: That means we are definitely fired, there is nothing left to lose.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'язательно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Точно, тебе обязательно нужен хороший врач.
examples.trans: Exactly, you definitely need a good doctor.

examples.text: Подождите, я обязательно с ней поговорю.
examples.trans: Wait, I will definitely talk to her.

examples.text: Хорошо, любимая, вечером обязательно приду домой.
examples.trans: Alright, darling, I will definitely come home tonight.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('needed').

examples.text: Нам тоже нужна статья!
examples.trans: We need an article too!

examples.text: Что тебе нужно, говори быстрее.
examples.trans: What do you need, speak faster.

examples.text: Чего тебе нужно в моём номере?
examples.trans: What do you need in my room?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good').

examples.text: Хорошо, иди, только не очень долго.
examples.trans: Alright, go, just not for very long.

examples.text: Точно, тебе обязательно нужен хороший врач.
examples.trans: Exactly, you definitely need a good doctor.

examples.text: Мой сын повар с хорошей зарплатой.
examples.trans: My son is a chef with a good salary.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Если я ещё могу помочь, просто скажи.
examples.trans: If I can still help, just say so.

examples.text: Сегодня не могу.
examples.trans: I can't today.

examples.text: Этого не может быть.
examples.trans: That can't be.

отвезти.gloss: to drive, to take (someone somewhere by vehicle)

meanings.en: to take, to drive (someone to a place)
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'везти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to drive, to take (someone somewhere by vehicle)', paired with 'отвозить'.

examples.text: Катя, можешь меня на рентген отвезти?
examples.trans: Katya, can you drive me to the X-ray?

examples.text: Потом обратно бесплатно отвезу.
examples.trans: Afterwards I'll drive you back for free.

examples.text: Отвезите меня в отель.
examples.trans: Drive me to the hotel.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'are afraid'.

examples.text: Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: We have nobody to fear here.

examples.text: Я не боюсь.
examples.trans: I'm not afraid.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она машину совсем не заметила.
examples.trans: She did not notice the car at all.

examples.text: Денис, дыши спокойно, сейчас вызовем скорую.
examples.trans: Denis, breathe calmly, we will call an ambulance now.

examples.text: Всё нормально, я просто конфетой подавился.
examples.trans: Everything is fine, I just choked on a candy.

meanings.en: to go by vehicle (habitually or round trip), to drive, to ride
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to drive, ride'.

examples.text: Если не боишься со мной ездить.
examples.trans: If you are not afraid to ride with me.

examples.text: Мы ездим на русских машинах.
examples.trans: We drive Russian cars.

examples.text: Он часто ездит в Москву.
examples.trans: He often goes to Moscow.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лично'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Одним словом, конкурент отлично держит марку.
examples.trans: In a word, the competitor holds his standard well.

examples.text: Отлично, тогда встретимся ровно через полчаса.
examples.trans: Great, then we will meet in exactly half an hour.

examples.text: Я этот город отлично знаю!
examples.trans: I know this town really well!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Атмосфера этого ресторана подкупает каждого гостя.
examples.trans: The atmosphere of this restaurant wins over every guest.

examples.text: Прекрасно, тогда я тебя очень жду.
examples.trans: Wonderful, then I am waiting for you eagerly.

examples.text: Отлично, тогда встретимся ровно через полчаса.
examples.trans: Great, then we will meet in exactly half an hour.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'третиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will meet', paired with 'встречаться'.

examples.text: Может, встретимся сейчас?
examples.trans: Maybe we could meet now?

examples.text: Встретимся в кафе.
examples.trans: Let's meet in the café.

examples.text: Аркаша, губернатор хочет с нами встретиться!
examples.trans: Arkasha, the governor wants to meet with us!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, можно вас на минуту?
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich, may I have a minute?

examples.text: Отлично, тогда встретимся ровно через полчаса.
examples.trans: Great, then we will meet in exactly half an hour.

examples.text: Всё очень вкусно, просто на высшем уровне.
examples.trans: Everything is very tasty, simply top-notch.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, after', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вы со вчерашнего дня ничего не ели.
examples.trans: You have not eaten anything since yesterday.

examples.text: Отлично, тогда встретимся ровно через полчаса.
examples.trans: Great, then we will meet in exactly half an hour.

examples.text: Через полчаса я буду готова.
examples.trans: In half an hour I will be ready.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лчаса'). Common masculine noun meaning 'half-hour' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Отлично, тогда встретимся ровно через полчаса.
examples.trans: Great, then we will meet in exactly half an hour.

examples.text: Через полчаса я буду готова.
examples.trans: In half an hour I will be ready.

examples.text: Соус заказали полчаса назад.
examples.trans: The sauce was ordered half an hour ago.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will be'.

examples.text: Ну, может быть, она просто влюбилась.
examples.trans: Well, maybe she simply fell in love.

examples.text: А я не могу так легко забыть.
examples.trans: And I cannot forget so easily.

examples.text: У меня есть машинка.
examples.trans: I have a toy car.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ready').

examples.text: Через полчаса я буду готова.
examples.trans: In half an hour I will be ready.

examples.text: Елена, к дегустации свадебного меню всё готово.
examples.trans: Elena, everything is ready for the wedding menu tasting.

examples.text: К обеду всё давно готово!
examples.trans: Everything has been ready for lunch for a long time!
